studies.label: Laboratory experiment: AI access crossed with incentive scheme

studies.task: Write a short creative composition about what one would create using thoughts alone, followed by an unassisted Divergent Association Test in the post-experimental questionnaire.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4.2
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4), Section 2.1, ChatGPT-4.2 API embedded in the experimental interface; confirmed in PDF p. 27 (printed p. 24), AI declaration. Model release year is not stated.

studies.shared_sample: The same laboratory experiment supplies a separate, unnamed study of Stage 2 competition choices. The paper does not identify that study or its exact analyzed overlap (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5, Section 2.1).

estimates.outcome: Average creativity score of the composition
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean of four independent ratings of each participant's composition by Italian-speaking Prolific evaluators, blind to treatment. Each text appears once in each presentation position. The main text says a 1 to 10 scale (PDF p. 9, printed p. 6, Section 2.2); laboratory and rater instructions say 0 to 10 (PDF p. 32, appendix p. 3; PDF p. 34, appendix p. 5). The minimum is unresolved.

regression.model: OLS with AI-access, Tournament, and Piece Rate indicators and an intercept; Lottery is the omitted incentive category. Full sample; no post-treatment covariates (Table 5, column (1)).

sources.locator: PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5, column (1), AI row and robust standard error; quote preserves all three AI-row columns in printed order.
PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5, column (1), Obs. row; notes identify columns (1)-(3) as the full sample.
PDF p. 16 (printed p. 13), Table 2, Obs. row: No-AI sample in column (4), AI sample in column (5). These are the AI-status counts for the same full sample used in Table 5.
PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5, significance legend; the AI coefficient in column (1) carries two stars.

estimates.notes: The paper calls the mean rating its main outcome (PDF p. 9, printed p. 6), but no preregistration is stated. The coefficient is the AI-access contrast adjusted only for randomized incentive indicators. Pooled arm means and participant SDs are not printed; the fitted intercept is not entered as an observed control mean. The table's F statistic and model p-value test the whole regression, so they are not entered as AI-contrast statistics. Reported uncertainty uses one observation per participant and robust SEs; adequacy of this precision depends on the unresolved individual-versus-session assignment unit.

estimates.outcome: Divergent Association Test (DAT) score after AI removal
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Average semantic distance between words supplied by the same participant, on a 0 to 100 scale with higher values indicating greater divergent thinking ability (PDF p. 14, printed p. 11, Table 1 notes). Within-person associative variety is coded as flexibility. The scoring model or embedding implementation is not specified.

estimates.notes: Although the authors interpret DAT as baseline creative potential, it was collected in the post-experimental questionnaire (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5). ChatGPT access ended when the composition was completed (PDF p. 31, appendix p. 2). Thus this is an immediate after_ai outcome, not an across_people diversity outcome. The elapsed delay is not printed. The coefficient is the AI-access contrast adjusted only for randomized incentive indicators. Pooled arm means and participant SDs are not printed; the fitted intercept is not entered as an observed control mean. The table's F statistic and model p-value test the whole regression, so they are not entered as AI-contrast statistics. Reported uncertainty uses one observation per participant and robust SEs; adequacy of this precision depends on the unresolved individual-versus-session assignment unit. No exact AI-coefficient p-value or significance bound is printed.

not_extracted.what: Average creativity score: adjusted AI-access coefficients in Table 2, columns (1) and (3).
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 16 (printed p. 13): these models control for composition length and DAT collected after assignment; column (3) additionally conditions on realized AI-query intensity. Excluded as post-treatment-adjusted effects. The eligible AI-access contrast in Table 5 is extracted instead.

not_extracted.what: Average creativity score: AI (use) and AI (no use) contrasts, Table 2, column (2).
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 16 (printed p. 13): active use is self-selected after assignment, and the model also includes post-treatment length and DAT controls. These are subgroup associations rather than full randomized-arm contrasts.

not_extracted.what: Creative-performance associations with query intensity, writing length, DAT, and participant characteristics, including Table 2 columns (3)-(5).
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 16 (printed p. 13): regressions on measured behaviors or characteristics, including analyses restricted by AI status, do not supply additional randomized AI-assistance contrasts.

not_extracted.what: Mediation models of Similarity and average creativity score, main Table 3.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 18 (printed p. 15): direct, indirect, and total effects use self-selected ideation requests and interaction behavior in the AI-access sample. Mediation analyses and effects conditioned on post-treatment mediators are excluded.

not_extracted.what: Mediation models using AI-first and User-first keywords, Appendix C Table 1.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 53 (printed appendix p. 24): mediation analyses of observed keywords and AI reliance, restricted to AI-access participants, do not estimate randomized AI-arm effects.

PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes; PDF p. 21 (printed p. 18), Table 4; PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5 column (4): sending a query is an adoption behavior, not creativity or diversity scored on participant-produced output.

not_extracted.what: Number of queries filled, including Tables 1, 4, and 5.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes; PDF p. 21 (printed p. 18), Table 4; PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5 column (5): interaction intensity counts prompts, not produced ideas or creative quality.

not_extracted.what: Similarity between a participant's final composition and that participant's AI responses.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes, and PDF p. 36 (printed appendix p. 7), Appendix B.4: TF-IDF cosine overlap measures incorporation of the participant's own AI responses. It does not compare different people's outputs and is not a creativity rating. Its mediation and incentive regressions therefore do not supply an across_people estimate.

not_extracted.what: Idea request and Idea request index, including Tables 1, 4, and 5.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes; PDF p. 36 (printed appendix p. 7), Appendix B; PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20), Table 5 columns (7)-(8): these classify requests for AI ideas and their intensity, not creativity scored on the final output. Realized request behavior is not randomized.

not_extracted.what: Books owned, AI exposure, gender, and determinants of AI usage.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes, and PDF p. 21 (printed p. 18), Table 4: participant characteristics and self-reports, and their associations with AI behavior, are not output-scored randomized AI-assistance outcomes.

not_extracted.what: Stage 2 competition choice and Stage 3 beliefs about own creativity score and rank.
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 5), Section 2.1: competition choice and expected performance are behaviors or beliefs, not creative output scores. Stage 2 analysis is assigned to a separate unnamed study; no eligible contrast for these outcomes is printed here.

not_extracted.what: Tournament and Piece Rate coefficients for creativity, composition length, and DAT in Table 5 columns (1)-(3).
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 23 (printed p. 20): these compare monetary incentive schemes while adjusting for AI access. They do not contrast AI assistance with a comparison or different AI configurations. Matched AI-versus-no-AI cells and the pooled AI-access coefficient are retained.

open_items: The number randomized, per-arm assignment-stage counts, exclusions, attrition, and reasons for unequal analyzed cell sizes are not reported separately (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5; PDF p. 14, printed p. 11, Table 1). Randomized counts remain null.

The treatment-assignment unit is unresolved: the paper states that participants were randomly assigned but also refers to sessions conducted under a treatment condition. Session counts by arm and allocation records are absent. Robust participant-level SEs are printed, but their adequacy under possible session assignment cannot be established (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5; PDF p. 23, printed p. 20).
The creativity-rating minimum conflicts: 1 to 10 in the main text versus 0 to 10 in both instruction sets (PDF p. 9, printed p. 6; PDF p. 32, printed appendix p. 3; PDF p. 34, printed appendix p. 5).

Combined AI and combined no-AI means and participant-level SDs are not printed for any extracted outcome. They were not calculated from the incentive-cell statistics. Table 5 intercepts are fitted baseline values, not observed pooled control means.

Exact AI-coefficient p-values, confidence intervals, and standardized effects are not printed in Table 5. Only the two-star p-value bounds are available for creativity and character count; no p-value is recorded for DAT.
The paper names the assistance model ChatGPT-4.2 but does not provide a release year or an API model identifier beyond that name (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4; PDF p. 27, printed p. 24). The year is null.
The separate Stage 2 competition-choice paper and its exact analyzed sample overlap are unidentified (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5).

External replication completeness is unresolved. Read-only urllib requests, with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, to https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/32132980 and the alternate named source https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/t93pf5r6fp/2 both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No replication files were downloaded or analyzed.

Rater payment is described as 3 Euro in the main text and 3 British pounds in the instructions; this does not affect the transcribed outcome contrasts (PDF p. 9, printed p. 6; PDF p. 34, printed appendix p. 5).
notes: Extracted on 2026-10-10. Read the entire markdown conversion sequentially, including Appendices A-C and final references, then checked cited pages with PyMuPDF text extraction. The survey-rater component scores the laboratory participants' outputs and is not counted as a separate AI-assistance study. One laboratory sample supplies all estimates. Every matched incentive-cell record includes its full analyzed arms. No cross-incentive comparisons were invented as AI-design contrasts. Pooled coefficients are from Table 5, whose only covariates are randomized incentive indicators; Table 2 AI coefficients are excluded because of post-treatment controls. The current codebook permits length for character counts and classifies within-person DAT variety as flexibility. No across_people outcome is reported. All numeric statistics are transcribed; no arm pooling, subtraction, standardization, p-value calculation, or count summation was performed. Source quotes preserve the paper's printed decimal precision and signs. Missing or unresolved values are null.
